keyVerseText: The fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst.
rootMeaning: The word χρυσόπρασος (chrysóprasos) combines χρυσός (chrysós), meaning 'gold,' with πράσον (práson), meaning 'leek.' This etymology suggests a precious stone that carries the golden quality of gold alongside the greenish tint reminiscent of a leek. Thus, the root meaning points to a gem distinguished by its golden-green color, emphasizing both value and a unique hue that sets it apart from ordinary gold or green stones alone.
usageInScripture: This term appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Revelation 21:20, where it is translated as 'a chrysoprasus.' Its singular occurrence and consistent translation as a precious stone highlight its role as a symbol of beauty and value rather than a common object. The use of this rare gemstone among other precious stones in the New Testament context underscores its significance as part of the description of the New Jerusalem's foundation.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding χρυσόπρασος as a golden-green gem enriches our appreciation of the New Jerusalem's foundation stones, symbolizing not only purity and value but also the multifaceted glory of God's eternal kingdom. The blending of gold's radiance with the greenish hue may reflect the vitality and life that come from God’s presence. This precious stone, set among others, points to the perfection and diversity of the redeemed community, secured by Christ’s work. It reminds believers that the eternal city is adorned with the richest and most beautiful treasures, signifying the surpassing worth of salvation and the hope of glory.
keyVerseReflection: Revelation 21:20 lists the chrysoprasus as the tenth foundation stone of the New Jerusalem, describing it alongside other precious gems. The inclusion of this golden-green gem emphasizes the splendor and richness of the heavenly city’s foundation. The word χρυσόπρασος contributes to the verse by evoking an image of radiant beauty and divine craftsmanship, reinforcing the vision of a perfect and glorious dwelling place prepared by God for His people.
